transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-22 10:00 UTC | Duration 55 min | Recording available
Attendees: Marta Lopez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Julia Chen (CTO - SynthMed), Mark Rivers (Platform Eng - SynthMed), Aisha Khan (Data Scientist - SynthMed)

[00:00] Marta Lopez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, is this still 55 minutes on your calendars? We can go 45 if folks are tight.
[00:12] Julia Chen: No, 55 is fine. We wanted to focus today on sizing and the autoscale behaviors, especially for bursty traffic from our web API.
[00:22] Samir Patel: Great. I'll run through the results from last week's perf runs and then we can talk policy thresholds and burst buckets.

[01:05] Samir Patel: So quick recap — we tested the 4-GPU pool with quantized 4-bit model and continuous batching. Baseline steady-state at 120 rps gave p50 around 95ms, p95 around 480ms, which lines up with what we expected. There was a cold-start path when cache was empty, p95 spiked to about 1.2s.
[01:48] Mark Rivers: When you say cache empty, do you mean KV cache or prefix cache? Our traffic is quite conversational so re-use is high but mornings are cold.
[02:10] Samir Patel: Yeah sorry, I mean the KV cache / prefix K V cache — the test zeroed caches before bursts. In the real traffic we should see much lower cold penalties after warmup but we need to account for long-tail users.

[04:00] Aisha Khan: Quick question — how does autoscaling handle mid-burst, like 3x our baseline for 30s? Will the system spin up extra instances and route requests during that time or queue?
[04:20] Samir Patel: Current Dedicated autoscaler supports fast ramp-up using pre-warmed burst capacity if you allocate a burst bucket. If not, it will spin up nodes which takes ~45-90s depending on instance type; so for sub-60s spikes we recommend a burst pool.
[05:05] Julia Chen: And the burst pool has cost implications, right? Do you charge for reserved burst or only when used?
[05:18] Marta Lopez: We do both options. You can reserve burst capacity (committed) for predictable bursts at a lower unit cost, or you can use elastic burst pay-as-you-go which has a premium. We'll include both in the quote.

[07:00] Samir Patel: Looking at the logs, the 8-GPU pool handled 600 rps steady with p95 ~420ms and cold restarts were less frequent because more front capacity allowed better KV cache hit rate across shards.
[07:35] Mark Rivers: So if we do 8-GPU pool, do we still get autoscale? I'm trying to map this to our SLO: p95 < 500ms for inference.
[07:50] Samir Patel: Yes, autoscale works at pool level; you can set min/max nodes and the autoscaler will keep you above SLO with policies like target latency or target utilization. For your p95 < 500ms target, Samir: recommend min 2 nodes, target util 60% and set a conservative scale-up cooldown to avoid oscillation.

[10:00] Julia Chen: I'm worried about oscillation during diurnal peaks — our traffic has sudden bursts from batch jobs at midnight UTC.
[10:18] Samir Patel: Right, for that pattern we recommend scheduled scaling + burst reserve. Scheduled will pre-scale before the midnight job. Burst bucket handles the short high-intensity spikes within the window. Also warm-up your KV cache with a short prefetch script to reduce cold-start penalties.

[12:30] Aisha Khan: How much of an impact does quantization have on accuracy for our biomedical prompts? We saw slight hallucination increases in a couple of tests.
[12:50] Samir Patel: Good flag — quantization can affect quality. Our Optimize team recommends A/B evals: run 4-bit quant and 8-bit quant side-by-side on your eval set. If quality degradation is unacceptable, you can use mixed precision — quantize embeddings but keep LM weights at 8-bit. We'll help set that up.

[15:00] Marta Lopez: We should align on cost/latency tradeoffs: 4-GPU pool with aggressive batching gives best cost per token but higher p95 under burst; 8-GPU pool gives better headroom. Which do you lean towards?
[15:22] Julia Chen: From product POV, p95 <500ms is required. If 4-GPU can't hit that consistently during our peak even with burst, we should look at 8-GPU.

[17:10] Samir Patel: Also note KV cache sharding matters. With 4 GPUs you have fewer shards so cache hit rates per node drop under cross-shard traffic. That explains some of the p95 degradation.
[17:45] Mark Rivers: Would session affinity help? We could sticky by user so requests hit same shard.
[18:03] Samir Patel: Session affinity helps a lot for conversational flows. We can configure affinity at the routing layer; downside is uneven load distribution if some users are much heavier.

[20:00] Julia Chen: For the stress test Samir mentioned, can you include a warmup phase and a ramp-down? Our last run terminated too fast and results were noisy.
[20:15] Samir Patel: Absolutely. Proposed test: 15m warmup, 2h steady at baseline, 5x spike for 3 minutes repeated 6 times with 10m recovery, then 15m cooldown. We'll record p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization and cache hit rates.
[20:45] Aisha Khan: Please also capture token per request distribution; some of our requests are 2k tokens which impacts throughput.

[23:00] Marta Lopez: On pricing — I'll prepare two quotes: (A) 4-GPU pool with reserved burst (B) 8-GPU pool with lower burst reserve. I'll include autoscale policy examples and expected monthly cost at your 120 rps baseline and at 3x burst.
[23:22] Mark Rivers: Can you also show cost per 1M tokens and the delta if we enable aggressive batching vs conservative batching?
[23:35] Marta Lopez: Yep, will include cost-per-token and an appendix with batching sensitivity.

[25:00] Julia Chen: Security quick note — we need SOC two compliance and KMS integration; we'll put a separate meeting to go through security docs.
[25:12] Marta Lopez: Understood, we'll send SOC 2 and the private Dedicated security sheet; happy to set a security review with our compliance team.

[28:00] Samir Patel: One more operational note — if you plan to do an on-prem/private deployment later, the same autoscale/burst model conceptually applies but spin-up times differ and you'd manage hardware pools. For now Dedicated in our hosted region gives faster elasticity.
[28:30] Mark Rivers: Noted. For the POC we want to simulate a future private deployment though so include that in run notes.

[31:00] Aisha Khan: A small nit — some of the logs in the last run show transcribed errors; we had a couple of 500s from the serving layer around the same time the autoscaler scaled.
[31:20] Samir Patel: That's probably connection churn during scale events; we'll instrument retries and graceful draining to minimize 500s.

[34:00] Julia Chen: Timeline check — if we get the stress results and updated quote this week, can we make a decision by early next week? We prefer to finalize capacity before end of month.
[34:15] Marta Lopez: Yes, if Mark uploads traces by Wednesday and Samir posts the stress report by Monday, we can have a follow-up decision call on Thursday.

[36:00] Mark Rivers: I'll upload traces and also add expected growth numbers.
[36:10] Marta Lopez: Great. Anything else on sizing?

[38:00] Samir Patel: Quick tactical: set autoscale scale-up threshold to target 60% GPU util, scale-down only after 10m cool-down, and enable a 2-node min for 8-GPU pool. For 4-GPU pool set min 1, but ensure burst pool covers short spikes.
[38:33] Julia Chen: For the burst pool, how do we size the bucket? Is it tokens per minute or nodes available?
[38:45] Samir Patel: It's configurable as extra nodes reserved for burst and as a credit bucket measured in node-seconds. We'll show examples in the runbook.

[41:00] Aisha Khan: Any notes about quantization fit for our biomedical use-case?
[41:12] Samir Patel: We'll run accuracy A/B and can recommend mixed precision if pure 4-bit fails. Also use prompt engineering to reduce hallucination risk.

[43:00] Marta Lopez: Recap next steps: Samir runs extended stress test and includes warmup/cooldown and token distribution; Marta sends pricing with autoscale and burst options; Mark uploads traces. If that all lands, we'll meet next Thursday for decision.

[44:15] Julia Chen: Sounds good. One ask — can you include an explicit example of the autoscale policy JSON or config? Our infra team prefers concrete samples.
[44:30] Samir Patel: Yes, I'll attach a sample policy (target latency, min/max nodes, cooldowns, burst bucket config). Note — sample may include internal field names but we'll annotate.

[47:00] Mark Rivers: Last question: can we run a short head-to-head of 4-GPU vs 8-GPU on our eval set to quantify accuracy + latency tradeoffs?
[47:18] Samir Patel: Yes, we can do that in the stress run; run both pools sequentially with identical traces.

[50:00] Marta Lopez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts: stress plan, policy sample, updated quote, and the security packet link.
[50:18] Julia Chen: Thanks all. Good sync.
[50:25] Mark Rivers: Thanks.
[50:30] Aisha Khan: Thanks.

[50:45] End of recording.
